name: Funeral home operations
hypothesis: DOS-era incumbents; documented $650/mo per-location pricing in indie-hacker examples. Tight, trust-based community though.

market_sizing.target_buyer: Funeral home owner/director (typically owner-operator at single-site independents; group-level operations director at small chains).
market_sizing.business_count_au: ~1,011 businesses in 'Funeral Directors, Crematoria and Cemeteries' in AU (IBISWorld 2025), growing 3.8% YoY. A broader count including related funeral-services companies is ~2,672. ICP (independent + small-chain funeral homes, excluding InvoCare/Propel) is roughly 600–800 buyers. State distribution: VIC ~30%, NSW ~29%, QLD ~15% (74% combined in top three).
market_sizing.business_count_global: US ~18,800 funeral homes (NFDA), UK ~4,500 funeral directors, Canada ~3,000. Global TAM is meaningful but each country has distinct regulation (death certificate flows, embalming licensure, preneed trust law) and a different incumbent set, so cross-border expansion requires localisation.
market_sizing.typical_size: Independent funeral home: 2–10 staff, 50–400 funerals/year, AUD $500k–$3M revenue. Small chains (3–10 locations) common but tier above ICP.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: Mixed. Modern entrants visible: Gather (US-origin) — one-time activation + monthly subscription, transparent. 1Director — $49/month. Funeral Buddy (AU) — $999 setup + $20/case. Passare — anecdotal $10k engagements (with cemetery add-ons). SRS Computing — anecdotal $2k–$5k annual licence per site + setup. FuneralOne — quote-only, multi-location enterprise. TerraPro, Osiris, MorTrack, PlotBox, byondpro, Tukios round out the field. The 'documented $650/mo per-location' figure in indie-hacker writeups appears in US contexts; closest AU comparables are SRS-style annual licences and Passare's higher tiers.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AU funeral homes are conservative buyers but the bigger independents pay $300–600/mo for software they trust. Sweet spot for new entrant: $200–450/mo single-location, with per-location uplift for chains.
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Outside sales / channel-heavy. Self-serve is unlikely to work — trust is paramount. Demos at NFDA/Funerals Australia events and direct relationships with industry consultants drive deals.
pricing_reality.realistic_arpu_au: AUD $300–500/month/location (lower than US per-location norms reflecting smaller AU case volumes).
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Strong 2–3x. Expansion via: (a) website/microsite tribute hosting (per-case), (b) live-streaming and memorial video (per-case), (c) embedded payments for at-need and preneed (high-value transactions), (d) preneed trust management module, (e) BDM/death-registry e-lodgement, (f) merchandise/casket/urn catalogue with ordering, (g) AI-drafted obituaries and orders-of-service. Embedded fintech is a particularly strong wedge — at-need invoices average AUD $7,000–12,000 with significant Stripe/AfterPay flow potential.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: 1) FuneralSoft (Instra Technologies, AU) — long-standing AU vendor. 2) Funeral Buddy (AU) — newer cloud entrant, transparent pricing. 3) Sacred Grounds — cloud, independent/family-run focus. 4) Passare (US) — cloud, present in AU via larger groups. 5) SRS Computing (US) — Procession/PROCession, established but legacy feel. 6) FuneralOne (US) — multi-location enterprise focus. 7) Gather (US) — modern UX, expanding. 8) Tukios (US) — tribute video + management. 9) TerraPro, Osiris, MorTrack, byondpro, PlotBox (cemetery-focused). Many AU independents still run paper + Excel + Word merge or legacy desktop tools.
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: Mixed. SRS Computing, FuneralOne, TerraPro >20 years (DOS lineage referenced in Passare migration anecdotes — Smartware-for-DOS 1988, FoxPro 1993). FuneralSoft ~15+ years. Gather ~10 years (founded 2014). Funeral Buddy newer. Dominant legacy players are >15 years old — strong UI rot signal.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: Capterra/G2 reviews and indie-hacker writeups consistently flag: dated UI on SRS/FuneralOne-class tools, slow vendor support, difficulty handling state-specific BDM forms, manual rekeying between case management and the funeral website, weak payments/AfterPay integration. Indie-hacker case studies (e.g. Parting Pro, smaller funeral-tech bootstrappers) have publicly documented bootstrapping success at per-location pricing — evidence the market pays. Reddit r/funeraldirectors has periodic 'what software are you on?' threads with widespread frustration.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Gather, Passare and Tukios have all taken growth capital in recent years (US). Parting Stone, Parting Pro and other deathcare-tech startups raised in 2023–2024. No high-profile AU-specific funeral SaaS funding in the last 12 months. Industry consolidation continues at the funeral-home level (Propel Funeral Partners growth) but vendor-side AU activity is quiet.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Low-to-moderate. AI obituary drafting and grief-support chatbots have appeared (Empathy.com etc.) but no AI-native end-to-end funeral-home SMS has emerged as dominant. Window is open ~18–24 months.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: Three intertwined unresolved workflows. (1) Case intake to BDM (Births Deaths Marriages) lodgement — currently paper/PDF forms re-keyed into the registry portal per state, with high error rates. (2) Order-of-service, tribute website and live-stream generation — manually assembled in Word/Canva/Vimeo per case. (3) At-need invoicing and payment collection — many homes still rely on EFT/manual receipts; AfterPay and split-payment between estate and family members is poorly handled. Spreadsheets + Word + Outlook + WhatsApp dominate the small end.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: Defensibility from: (a) state-by-state BDM integration depth (each state has its own portal — e.g. NSW LifeLink, VIC BDM Online, QLD BDM), (b) cemetery/crematorium scheduling integrations, (c) coroner/medical-certificate workflow, (d) accumulated case templates and order-of-service designs, (e) embedded payments stickiness, (f) deep insider trust within a tight community.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Must: state BDM e-lodgement portals (8 jurisdictions), Xero/MYOB, Stripe + AfterPay/Zip for at-need payments, SMS, email/Mailchimp, live-stream (Vimeo/Restream), e-signature. Strongly desired: cemetery booking APIs, coffin/casket supplier catalogues, florist integrations, hearse/transport scheduling, preneed trust management.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Low at the small/independent end (paper + spreadsheets dominate). Moderate at the mid/chain end where Passare/FuneralOne hold case history. Side-car wedges (e.g. payments + tribute website + BDM lodgement) viable; full rip-and-replace is hard.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: Moderate. State-by-state BDM lodgement requirements, coroner referral rules, embalming/mortuary licensing (varies by state), cemetery and crematorium booking. No federal regulator equivalent to NDIS Commission/ASQA. Industry self-regulates heavily via AFDA/NFDA codes.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: Weaker forcing functions than NDIS or RTO. No federally mandated 2026 deadline. Ongoing modernisation of state BDM portals (NSW, VIC) creates integration opportunities but not a forced-churn event. Some state-level reviews of funeral-industry pricing transparency (Funeral Industry Code reviews) are ongoing — could create a documentation/transparency wedge but not a sharp deadline.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: Deep and culturally sensitive. Outsider needs a domain co-founder or operator partnership to be credible. Trust-based community where word-of-mouth dominates. ~9–12 months to credible fluency without an insider.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 6–9 months for a narrow wedge (e.g. case intake + BDM lodgement + tribute site). Full SMS replacement is 12–18 months.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: Moderate. Hard problems: state BDM portal integrations (some are not API-first; may need RPA-style automation), live-stream reliability for funeral services (zero-failure expectation), cemetery scheduling, multi-jurisdiction death-certificate forms, preneed trust accounting (regulated financial product in some states).
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: High. Each state/territory has its own BDM registry, coroner rules, cremation permit forms, and mortuary licensing. ~8 rule engines needed for full national coverage.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Yes — sensitive personal data of the deceased and bereaved; AU hosting expected and explicitly preferred.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: (1) AFDA (Funerals Australia) and NFDA member partnerships and conference exhibits — the dominant channel. (2) State funeral directors associations (FDA NSW merged into NFDA in 2024). (3) Outside sales / regional sales reps with industry references. (4) Word-of-mouth via early-adopter funeral directors. (5) Content/SEO is weak — directors don't Google for software, they ask peers. (6) Coffin/casket and stationery supplier partnerships (these reps visit every home). (7) Cold outbound viable but conversion is slow.
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: 3–4 active: Funerals Australia (formerly AFDA, founded 1935, national), NFDA (National Funeral Directors Association of Australia, ~200 members post-FDA-NSW merger 2024), state cemeteries/crematoria associations, Australasian Cemeteries and Crematoria Association (ACCA).
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: Very few — AFDA/Funerals Australia journal, NFDA newsletter, Australian Cemeteries and Crematoria Review. ~2–3 with paid sponsorship inventory.
distribution_difficulty.industry_facebook_group_size: Small. Funeral-director Facebook groups are private and modest (low hundreds to low thousands). LinkedIn presence is also modest. Community is offline-first and relationship-based.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: 2–4/year: AFDA/Funerals Australia National Convention, NFDA conference, ACCA conference, state-level forums. Booths typically <$10K. Attending all of them is feasible and almost essential.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: Moderate. ABN/contact lists for funeral homes are obtainable (Yellow Pages-grade) but response rates are low without a warm intro or industry reference. Phone outbound works better than email.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Low for a pure technologist outsider. Funeral directors trust other funeral directors. An insider co-founder, advisor, or owned reference site is close to a prerequisite. This is the single biggest distribution risk in this opportunity.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: High. First 5 reference customers may take 6–12 months and likely require free implementation + heavy hand-holding. Acquisition cost meaningfully higher than NDIS/RTO.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Low crowding but also low buyer search volume — directors don't research software via Google. SEO is not the primary acquisition lever here.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: State BDM portals are the key gatekeeper — some accept third-party integrations, others don't. Cemetery/crematorium booking systems vary. No insurer gatekeeper, but preneed insurance products (Foresters Friendly, Sureplan) are relevant for the preneed module.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: ~15–25%. Multi-tenant org/site, staff, RLS, audit log, document store, suppliers (caskets/flowers ≈ Manuva supplier model), purchase orders (casket POs) reuse cleanly. Case management, body/disposition workflow, tribute sites are new.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Auth, tenant context, RLS, server actions, invite flow, activity logging, design tokens transfer. Supplier/PO module from Manuva (goods-inwards, supplier filtering) maps to casket/urn/flower ordering surprisingly well.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: None. Manuva sells to manufacturers, not funeral homes. No bundle/expansion play.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Very low. Different buyer, different culture, different regulator. Only platform-level reuse plus the supplier/PO sub-model.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 12–18 months. State BDM integrations and accumulated trust extend defensibility; pure SaaS shell replicable inside a year. Real moat is relational/cultural, not technical.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Healthy on subscription. Risk: live-streaming bandwidth costs (~$5–20/service), AI obituary inference (negligible), SMS/notification flow. Payments revenue is high-margin if embedded fintech is added. ~80–85% gross margin sustainable.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Moderate. Independents may grow to 2–3 locations; large groups (InvoCare, Propel) are out of ICP. Per-location expansion is real but caps at a handful per customer.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Low. Funeral homes are multi-generational, stable businesses with low business mortality. Once trust is established and case history is in-system, churn is very low (likely <5% annually).
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: At AUD $400/mo single-location ARPU = $4,800/yr → ~210 customers for $1M ARR. With ~600–800 ICP, that is ~30% market penetration — feasible only with strong insider channel.
